profile.campus: Chandler, Maricopa County, Arizona (CyrusOne Phoenix-metro campus, PHX1-PHX8)
profile.address: 2605 South Ellis Street, Building 8, Chandler, AZ 85286
profile.reading:
CyrusOne PHX6 is Building 8 on CyrusOne's Chandler, Arizona campus, addressed at 2605 South Ellis Street, Chandler, AZ 85286. It is one of eight buildings on a single roughly 2,000,000 square foot campus, numbered PHX1 through PHX8, that CyrusOne states carries 169 MW of power capacity in total. That combined figure describes the whole eight-building site, not any one building on it, and CyrusOne has not published a separate megawatt or square footage figure for PHX6.

The Chandler campus grew in phases starting in the early 2010s. CyrusOne's own materials and Data Center Knowledge's coverage from that period describe PHX1 opening in February 2013 with roughly 150,000 square feet of shell space and about 80,000 square feet of operational data center space at 28 MW, PHX2 following in 2014 at a smaller scale, roughly 60,000 square feet of shell holding about 35,000 square feet of data center space at 6 MW, and PHX3 breaking ground in June 2015 with a planned 120,000 square foot shell whose final power allocation was not set at the time. CyrusOne has not published comparable per-building detail for the later additions to the campus, including PHX6, so this record does not assign it an individual capacity or footprint figure.

Design standards published for the whole campus include a TIA 942 Class 4 rating, described as capable of exceeding 1,000 watts per square foot of usable floor, and a 36 inch raised floor system. Certification claims vary across the eight buildings. PHX6 falls outside both the Energy Star group, limited to PHX3 and PHX4, and the Green Globe Three Globes group, limited to PHX1 through PHX5, so this record does not claim either certification for this building. NWF Certified Wildlife Habitat status covers all eight buildings on the campus, PHX1 through PHX8, including PHX6.

CyrusOne itself has changed hands several times. Dave Ferdman founded the company in Texas in 2000 as a high density colocation provider for energy sector customers in Houston and Dallas. Private equity firm ABRY Partners bought the company in 2007, and Cincinnati Bell acquired it for 525 million dollars in 2010. Cincinnati Bell then spun CyrusOne off as a public real estate investment trust through a January 2013 initial public offering. The public company grew for nearly a decade until 2022, when investment firms KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners took it private again in an all cash deal. Shareholders were paid 90.50 dollars per share, a premium of about 2.5 percent to the prior closing price, and the deal was valued near 15 billion dollars including assumed debt. The two firms announced the transaction closed on March 25, 2022.

CyrusOne today is headquartered at 2850 North Harwood Street in Dallas and describes its current footprint as more than 60 data centers across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia Pacific, up from the roughly 40 facilities and 4 million square feet the company reported around the time of the take private deal. Its business is wholesale and colocation, leasing built capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale customers rather than operating its own end user cloud service, the same model followed by peers such as Digital Realty and QTS.

The Chandler campus sits in the Phoenix metro, one of the larger secondary United States data center markets, a status trade press attributes partly to electricity costs below California and the Pacific Northwest, Arizona's comparatively low natural disaster exposure with limited seismic activity and no hurricane risk, and state tax treatment for data center equipment. Eight buildings on one site sharing one utility connection give CyrusOne flexibility to lease Chandler capacity to multiple tenants at different scales, from smaller colocation footprints up to larger blocks, though nothing published here indicates PHX6 specifically is configured for large single tenant AI training clusters rather than general multi tenant colocation.

reading.body:
CyrusOne PHX6 is one building in an eight-building Chandler campus totaling roughly 2 million square feet. The operator publishes 169 MW of IT capacity across the entire PHX1-PHX8 campus, but does not confirm how that capacity distributes among individual buildings, so this building's own load cannot be stated here. At an assumed 15 kW per rack, a conservative estimate for mixed colocation workloads, 169 MW campus-wide would support roughly 11,300 racks across all eight buildings.

This campus ranks fifth among Arizona facilities with published capacity figures. Arizona's published data center capacity totals 512 MW across four facilities with disclosed specifications, and CyrusOne's Chandler campus alone represents 33 percent of that state total. The state has 56 mapped data center facilities overall, meaning most publish no capacity data.

Chandler's appeal to large operators stems from low natural-disaster risk, state tax treatment favorable to data center equipment, and fiber connectivity to Los Angeles and West Coast peering points. The site draws power from Salt River Project, which also serves hyperscale growth in the Phoenix metro that has made Arizona a secondary US hub for data centers. Water-intensive cooling in an arid state remains a regional constraint that local outlets have flagged, though site-specific consumption for this campus is not published.
